rubrics.criterion: The query-pair extraction routine no longer builds its per-pair work in place: pair normalization (URL-decode then re-encode with first-'=' handling), decoded-copy construction, pair storage bookkeeping and the '+ is a space' decoding scan run through single-purpose helper functions called from the extraction loop, using the existing helpers or equivalents with the same scoping.
rubrics.rationale: This loop is the deepest chain in the ingestion path; its copies are the core of what the task asks to untangle, and leaving any of the four steps inline keeps the extraction routine implementing its sub-routines.

rubrics.criterion: The command-line query update routine no longer carries the pair-normalization/decoding work of the pair pipeline inline; it delegates to the same shared normalization helpers again based on key/value matching and update semantics preserved.
rubrics.rationale: The update path duplicated the same responsibilities as ingestion with its own local copies; the pipeline is only consistent when both sides delegate to one implementation.

rubrics.criterion: The per-URL component mutation loop delegates again: single-component mutation (pre-check, encode/conditional option composition, IPv6 host handling, the underlying URL mutation call and its diagnostics) and component-name resolution are performed by helper functions, and the mutation loop only orchestrates per assignment.
rubrics.rationale: The --set driver fused two nested helper responsibilities into its loop; the desired abstraction is that the driver calls one setter that itself resolves names at the right level.

rubrics.criterion: Both per-URL output paths (default full-URL printing and the JSON per-component loop) fetch URL parts through one shared flag-composing fetch helper again, including the bad-hostname conversion retry, instead of duplicated inline flag computations and retry sequencing.
rubrics.rationale: Option-sensitive flag composition existed at two main output sites as two copies; unifying them through the helper is the direct reason this cleanup matters.

rubrics.criterion: The JSON params emission escapes pair keys and values through the shared JSON string-escaping function again (or an equivalent single shared escaper used for all JSON string output), instead of expanded inline copies of the escape dispatch.
rubrics.rationale: Two pasted variants of an escaping policy in one output function are the classic drift source; a single shared escaping path is the concrete outcome requested.

rubrics.criterion: The restored delegation preserves each call site's option semantics: the JSON component loop still requests the URL-encoded representation and suppresses decoding exactly where it did before, and the default output path fetches with the same default-port, keep-port, encoding-preference and non-support-scheme behavior as before the cleanup.
rubrics.rationale: Reconnecting helpers is only correct if the modifiers/options each caller passed before the flattening are threaded back through; silently dropping or hardcoding them changes output even when the structure looks right.

rubrics.criterion: Cross-function pair-pipeline state propagation is intact after the repair: pair storage slots, the stored normalized/decoded pair contents and the re-encoded-difference ("modified") detection still operate identically across ingestion and update paths.
rubrics.rationale: The inline copies interleaved with pair-state and modification bookkeeping; restoring delegation must not change how stored pair state and modification flags interact.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair, each responsibility has a single authority: no output or query path retains a private variant of the fetch-flag composition, pair normalization or string escaping that differs from the shared implementation the other paths use.
rubrics.rationale: The end state the task requests is one shared implementation per step; a repair that centralizes some paths but leaves one private copy has only moved the problem.

rubrics.criterion: The duplicated inline blocks are fully removed rather than left behind in a disguised form: no commented-out copies of the pasted fragments, no unreachable branches reproducing them, and no dead locals or labels left from the extraction.
rubrics.rationale: Half-done extraction that keeps the copies in non-executing form still costs comprehension and review effort, which is the exact cost this task exists to remove.

rubrics.criterion: No helper is orphaned by the repair: newly introduced extraction helpers are actually called on every path they were created for, and pre-existing helpers that still have their other callers keep those callers rather than being deleted or left unreferenced.
rubrics.rationale: The pipeline's helpers legitimately serve cold paths; deleting them (or stranding them unused) either breaks behavior outright or leaves the dead-code breakage the strict flags build already rejects.

rubrics.criterion: Query-pair decoding keeps interpreting a bare '+' as a space strictly on the undecoded side, while an encoded plus (%2B) survives as a literal '+' in stored and emitted values.
rubrics.rationale: Moving decode steps across helper boundaries can accidentally apply space promotion to already-decoded values or skip it where it is required; this quirk is the most fragile boundary in the pair logic.

rubrics.criterion: Null bytes in decoded pair copies keep being converted only for the display forms that convert them, with the stored pair contents unaffected.
rubrics.rationale: The conversion is output-context dependent and sits inside one of the pasted fragments; an extraction that makes it unconditional (or drops it) changes emitted output silently.

rubrics.criterion: Pair storage discipline is unchanged: empty query-pair segments still occupy pair slots with empty contents, and the pair-capacity bound and its warning stay exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: Slot bookkeeping is interleaved with the pasted storage fragment; re-scoping helpers can reorder the slot lifecycle and change outputs for queries with empty segments.

rubrics.criterion: The bad-hostname conversion retry remains a single retry in every path that fetches URL parts, and the conversion option remains disabled for the remainder of the run afterwards, as it was with the helper-owned behavior.
rubrics.rationale: The retry contains a persistent option mutation; helper re-scoping is the natural place to lose either the retry budget or the persistence.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not turn option-driven behavior unconditional: part fetching must not become always-decode or always-encode regardless of the tool's encoding preference, and the component mutation's conditional pre-check must not become unconditional.
rubrics.rationale: Simplifying away the option plumbing is the most tempting shortcut once flag composition is centralized, and it changes outputs only for some URLs, making it easy to miss.
